title: Frustum of Cone, Pyramid & Combined 3D Solids (Advanced Mensuration)
summary: Masterclass on truncated solids, Frustum slant heights, volume formulas, composite solids, and cavity drilling invariants with 3-tier solutions...

items: **Frustum of a Right Circular Cone (radii (R, r); vertical height (h)):**
**Curved Surface Area (CSA):** (	ext{CSA} = pi (R + r) l)
**Total Surface Area (TSA):** (	ext{TSA} = pi (R + r) l + pi R^2 + pi r^2)
**Volume ((V)):** (V =  rac{1}{3} pi h (R^2 + r^2 + R cdot r))

**Drilling a conical/cylindrical cavity from a solid:** Volume decreases ((V_{	ext{remaining}} = V_{	ext{solid}} - V_{	ext{cavity}})), but **Total Surface Area increases** because the internal curved walls of the cavity are now exposed ((	ext{TSA}_{	ext{new}} = 	ext{TSA}_{	ext{solid}} - 	ext{Base Area} + 	ext{CSA}_{	ext{cavity}})).
**Surmounting a hemisphere on a cylinder:** Total Volume (= V_{	ext{cyl}} + V_{	ext{hemi}}); Total Surface Area (= 	ext{CSA}_{	ext{cyl}} + 	ext{Base}_{	ext{cyl}} + 	ext{CSA}_{	ext{hemi}}).

blocks.content: 🎯 Exam Angle → ⚡ Frustum Volume Memory Anchor: Notice the term ((R^2 + r^2 + Rr)) in the Frustum volume formula — it is the algebraic expansion quotient from ( rac{R^3 - r^3}{R - r}). When (r = 0), it perfectly collapses to the standard Cone volume ( rac{1}{3}pi R^2 h).
